data.bug_class: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds READ via missing length clamp in checksum computation)
data.rationale: Confirmed by running the built fuzz target (/out/fuzz via run_poc.sh, and an equivalent libFuzzer build) under ASan: an ICMP echo packet triggers a 1-byte READ past the end of the TX buffer in csumup(). Reachability: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput (test/fuzz.c:81) calls mip_rx() with raw attacker bytes; mip_rx() (mip.c:770-775) dispatches eth type 0x800 to rx_ip(), which for proto==1 calls rx_icmp() (mip.c:703-707). In rx_icmp, for an echo (type==8) whose IP dst matches ifp->ip (0 in the harness), the code copies only `left = min(pkt->pay.len, tx space)` payload bytes into the TX buffer (mip.c:452-455), but line 457 then computes `icmp->csum = ipcsum(icmp, sizeof(*icmp) + pkt->pay.len)` using the UNCLAMPED pay.len. csumup() (mip.c:233-237) therefore walks sizeof(struct icmp)+pay.len bytes starting at `icmp`, which lives in ifp->tx.buf (the harness's VLA `char t[sizeof(struct mip_if)+1540*2]`, fuzz.c:63). When pay.len exceeds the remaining TX room (1540 - 42 = 1498 bytes, i.e. a frame larger than 1540 bytes), the read runs past the end of that buffer. ASan reports the crash at mip.c:236 via ipcsum <- rx_icmp <- rx_ip <- mip_rx <- LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput. The root cause is line 457 using pkt->pay.len instead of the clamped `left`; upstream fixed it by passing `left` to ipcsum.
